content.key_idea: PIPM extends MSI cache coherence with two migration-aware states (ME, I') encoded via directory state plus an in-memory bit, adding six new host/device transitions.
content.reading_order: Left to right: directory/DRAM block diagrams, then the two state-encoding tables, then the host-side and device-side numbered transition diagrams.

style.arrows: thin arrows with solid triangular heads; small filled circled numbers (1-6) badge specific transitions

encoding.color_means: red marks the new PIPM states (ME, I') and their table cells; black is used for the pre-existing M/S/I states
encoding.line_style_means: dashed arrows are the default (pre-existing) MSI transitions; solid arrows are the six new Extra (migration-related) transitions
encoding.state_means: new vs existing states are told apart by red vs black text/outline on the same circle-and-arrow diagram
encoding.marker_means: small filled circles numbered 1-6 identify each of the six newly introduced host-side/device-side transitions
encoding.emphasis: red is reserved exclusively for the new ME/I' states, repeated identically across both tables and both transition graphs

evidence: we introduce an additional per-cache-block in-memory bit in both local and CXL memory
local writeback operations (case 1) that initiate incremental migration from CXL memory to a host's local memory
By default, the in-memory bit is initialized to 0

summary: Figure 9 documents PIPM's extension to MSI cache coherence for multi-host CXL disaggregated shared memory. Stacked block diagrams on the left show the host's Local Coherence Directory and DRAM (tracking migrated lines) above the CXL Device Coherence Directory and DRAM (tracking non-migrated lines), gated by inter-host and local read/write/writeback requests. Two tables encode PIPM's new per-block in-memory bit alongside directory state: locally, Default (M/S/I, bit 0) versus Extra (ME/I', bit 1); at the device, Default (M/S/I, bit 0) versus Extra (I', bit 1), new states shown in red. On the right, two circle-and-arrow diagrams show host-side and device-side transitions among M, S, I, ME and I', with six newly introduced, numbered transitions added to the default dashed MSI triangle to support partial, incremental migration triggered by events such as a local writeback.
